office_does: A King County Councilmember writes county laws, adopts the county budget and oversees services such as Metro Transit, public health, the jail and the Sheriff's Office.
race_blurb: Open seat left by now-Executive Girmay Zahilay. State Sen. Rebecca Saldaña led the primary with 56% over Port Commissioner Toshiko Grace Hasegawa's 35%; both are progressive Democrats with overlapping endorsements, and they differ more in experience and detail than in direction.

candidates.summary: State Senator for the 37th District since 2016 and Senate Labor & Commerce chair, former Puget Sound Sage director, running on taxing the ultra-wealthy, universal child care, transit and housing.
highlights: Senator since 2016; chairs the Senate Labor & Commerce Committee [S1][S8]
Sponsored and voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million (ESSB 6346), the law I-645 would repeal [S4][S5]
Cites the capital gains tax, Paid Family and Medical Leave and the Domestic Workers Bill of Rights as her record [S1][S3]
Says the county must ensure "not a single penny" aids ICE; co-chaired the state jail-standards task force [S7]
Sole endorsement of the King County Democrats; endorsed by The Urbanist and The Stranger in the primary [S1][S9][S10]

taxes.basis: Sponsored and voted for the 2026 income tax on income over $1 million, cites the capital gains tax, and campaigns on taxing the ultra-wealthy.

spending.basis: Campaigns on universal child care, expanded behavioral health and crisis response, and fast, free transit funded by new revenue.

housing.basis: Wants housing affordable at any income, defends Housing First and cites anti-displacement and homeownership programs; was more hesitant than her opponent about a county social-housing levy.

safety.basis: Prioritizes community-based crime prevention, behavioral-health investment and crisis response; no enforcement-first proposals in the dossier.

climate.basis: Prime sponsor of the HEAL Act and credits herself with the Climate Commitment Act and Clean Fuel Standard; says 'we have put a price on carbon.'

experience.basis: Ten years in the state Senate with a committee chair and a record of sponsored and enacted laws.

candidates.summary: Port of Seattle Commissioner since 2022 and 2025 commission president, former director of the state Commission on Asian Pacific American Affairs, running on anti-displacement, social housing, child care and justice-system reform.
highlights: Port of Seattle Commissioner since 2022 and commission president in 2025; earlier led a state commission in Gov. Inslee's cabinet [S2][S6]
Would lobby to lift the 1% property-tax cap, supports a countywide housing levy and high-earner excise taxes [S4]
Proposes social housing at scale, land banking near transit and a "Stay Housed Guarantee" [S4]
Supports LEAD diversion, a zero youth incarceration goal and full subpoena power for the county's police-oversight office [S4][S7]
Endorsed by Executive Zahilay, former Governors Inslee and Locke, and the Seattle Times (primary) [S1][S5][S6]

taxes.basis: Would lobby to lift the 1% property-tax cap and pursue high-earner excise taxes and a progressive county B&O tax, and backs a countywide housing levy.

spending.basis: Platform expands county programs (social housing, child-care subsidies capped at 10% of income, a public bank) while pairing them with audit and accountability measures.

housing.basis: Detailed platform for social housing at scale, county land for permanently affordable housing, renter legal counsel, eviction prevention and a right to return.

safety.basis: Platform centers on LEAD and pre-trial diversion, a zero youth incarceration goal, ending pretextual traffic stops and stronger police oversight, plus community gun-violence prevention.

climate.basis: Opposes adding car lanes on Rainier Ave S. and backs lidding I-5 to reduce pollution; Inslee credits her Port 'Teal New Deal' work, but she would put bus service ahead of fleet electrification.

experience.basis: Current elected Port commissioner (since 2022, president in 2025) and former state commission director: an executive record, shorter than her opponent's legislative tenure.
